title: Measuring the reach of “fake news” and online disinformation in Europe (RISJ factsheet, February 2018; Fletcher, Cornia, Graves & Nielsen). Manifest title — “In France and Italy, the so-called ‘fake news’ have a limited reach, new study reveals” — is a press-release rendering of this same study.
screen_reason: Reports quantitative shares with a denominator: the average monthly reach (share of the online population visiting at least once) of websites identified by independent fact-checkers as publishers of false news, in France and Italy, from comScore behavioural measurement — a REACH estimate under the review's criteria. Note the text is the RISJ factsheet itself rather than the news item named in the manifest, but it is the same study and the same numbers.

estimates.platform: False news websites (comScore web audience measurement)
estimates.date: January, April, July and October 2017 (average of the four months)
estimates.measure_type: % of the French online population that visited the single most-reached false news website (Sante+ Magazine) in an average month of 2017
estimates.value_raw: 3.1% (≈ 1.5 million people); Appendix Table 1 monthly figures 5.8 / 2.2 / 2.6 / 1.9, Avg. 3.1
estimates.denominator: French online population measured by comScore (denominator size not stated; 3.1% is said to equate to around 1.5 million people)
estimates.definition: Visited, in an average month of 2017, a website on the filtered Decodex category-2 list ("websites that have published a significant amount of false information")
estimates.misinfo_def: "for-profit fabrication, politically-motivated fabrication [and] malicious hoaxes" designed to masquerade as news (Nielsen and Graves 2017)
estimates.n: French online population (comScore panel + server-side measurement); size not reported
estimates.source_quote: The most popular, Santé+ Magazine—an outlet that has been shown by Les Décodeurs to publish demonstrably false health information—reached 3.1% (this equates to around 1.5 million people).
estimates.page_loc: Results — France, p. 3; Appendix Table 1, p. 9 (www.santeplusmag.com)
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Le Monde's Décodex database (~1000 sites compiled by the Décodeurs fact-checking project), restricted to category 2 (sites that have published a significant amount of false information); satirical sites, questionable-verification sites and news sites excluded; RT and Sputnik displayed separately. No coder-reliability statistics reported.
estimates.moderator_quote: For both France and Italy, our starting point was lists of unreliable websites compiled by independent factcheckers and other observers. For France, we used the Décodex—a database of around 1000 websites compiled by Le Monde's Décodeurs project in the course of their fact-checking.
estimates.notes: KEY CAVEAT FOR THE ADJUDICATOR: this is the reach of ONE outlet (the most-visited false news site), not the combined reach of the false-news category — the factsheet never reports a combined/unduplicated reach across sites, so no category-level prevalence is extractable. The paper's own summary bound is "None of the false news websites we considered had an average monthly reach of over 3.5% in 2017, with most reaching less than 1% of the online population in both France and Italy"; I did not make that a separate row because it is a bound over the same per-site figures. denom_selection=curated reflects the top-20 rank-truncated presentation of a fact-checker-curated site list; the denominator itself is the national online population (REACH → denom_scope population). borderline=true flags the single-outlet scope, not doubt about the number, which is verbatim in both text and appendix table.

estimates.platform: False news websites (comScore web audience measurement)
estimates.date: January, April, July and October 2017 (average of the four months)
estimates.measure_type: % of the Italian online population that visited the single most-reached false news website (Retenews24) in an average month of 2017
estimates.value_raw: 3.1% (just over 1 million people); Appendix Table 2 monthly figures 4.2 / 5.1 / 2.7 / 0.5, Avg. 3.1
estimates.denominator: Italian online population measured by comScore (denominator size not stated; 3.1% is said to be just over 1 million people)
estimates.definition: Visited, in an average month of 2017, a website on the fact-checker lists of Italian sites that have repeatedly published demonstrably false information (satirical sites removed)
estimates.misinfo_def: "for-profit fabrication, politically-motivated fabrication [and] malicious hoaxes" designed to masquerade as news (Nielsen and Graves 2017)
estimates.n: Italian online population (comScore panel + server-side measurement); size not reported
estimates.source_quote: In Italy, the most widely-used false news website in our sample—Retenews24—reached 3.1% of the online Italian population (just over 1 million people) on average each month (see Figure 4).
estimates.page_loc: Results — Italy, p. 5; Appendix Table 2, p. 10 (www.retenews24.it)
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Three independently compiled Italian lists — BUTAC, Bufale and Bufalopedia — of sites that have repeatedly published demonstrably false information; satirical sites excluded; Sputnik Italy displayed separately. No coder-reliability statistics reported.
estimates.moderator_quote: In Italy, we combined lists from three different sources. Two of these lists were retrieved from independent fact-checking websites—BUTAC and Bufale. The third list came from Bufalopedia, a website co-created by Paolo Attivissimo... These are the best available, independently-compiled lists of websites that have repeatedly published demonstrably false information.
estimates.notes: Same caveat as the French row: a single outlet's monthly reach, not the reach of the false-news category as a whole. Italy's site pool after filtering was 21 sites, of which the top 20 are shown. The 3.1% for Retenews24 is an average of four very different months (4.2, 5.1, 2.7, 0.5) — the site collapsed during 2017; the average is the paper's own headline figure.

missed_or_uncertain: NOT extracted, with reasons. (1) Time-spent figures (Santé+ Magazine ~9.4 million minutes/month in France; the best Italian site 7.5 million minutes; Le Monde 172.8 million; La Repubblica 443.5 million) are absolute totals with no denominator, so they are neither a proportion nor a per-capita intensity — no row is possible. (2) Facebook interaction counts (Santé+ Magazine 11.3 million/month; La Gauche m'a Tuer ~1.5 million; Io Vivo a Roma 720,000) are counts, not shares. (3) Audience-overlap figures — "45.4% of Santé+ Magazine users also used Le Figaro in October 2017, and 34% used Le Monde"; "62.2% of Retenews24 users also visited the website of Il Corriere della Sera, and 52.3% used La Repubblica" — are shares of a false-news site's own audience overlapping with mainstream news, not shares of misinformation exposure; they answer a different question and I judged them out of scope. (4) RT (1.7% avg in the appendix table, quoted as 1.5% in the running text — a discrepancy worth noting) and Sputnik (France 1.4%, Italy 0.6%) are deliberately held apart by the authors as Décodex category 3 (questionable verification), not category 2 false news, so I did not code them as misinformation reach. (5) Every other per-site reach value in Appendix Tables 1 and 2 is available (38 French and 21 Italian sites filtered, top 20 shown per country) if the review ever wants site-level rows; I kept only the maximum per country per R4. (6) No combined or unduplicated reach across false-news sites is reported anywhere in the factsheet — the authors explicitly flag the untracked 'long tail' as a limitation.

rob.design: comScore panel + server-side measurement of website use in France and Italy, averaged over January, April, July and October 2017; false-news sites taken from independent fact-checker lists (Décodex category 2 in France; BUTAC, Bufale, Bufalopedia in Italy), then filtered to remove satire, standalone social accounts, hosted blogs and sites too small for comScore, leaving 38 sites in France and 21 in Italy with the top 20 per country reported; Facebook interactions from CrowdTangle; no response rate, no coder-reliability statistics (site classification is third-party fact-checkers').
rob.item6_quote: Here, we are concerned with outlets that consistently and deliberately publish “false news”, which we have defined elsewhere as “for-profit fabrication, politically-motivated fabrication [and] malicious hoaxes” designed to masquerade as news (Nielsen and Graves 2017).
rob.item10_quote: The most popular, Santé+ Magazine—an outlet that has been shown by Les Décodeurs to publish demonstrably false health information—reached 3.1% (this equates to around 1.5 million people).
